chunks: Muhammad, from Ahmad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Jameel bin Salih, from Zareeh who said:

I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) seeking refuge for one of his sons, and he was saying: 'I am resolved against you, O wind, and O pain, whatever you are, with the determination with which Ali bin Abi Talib, the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him), Messenger of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), resolved against the Jinn of Wadi al-Sabrah. So they answered and obeyed. You answer and obey, and go out from my son so-and-so, son of my daughter so-and-so, at this moment, at this moment.'
ai.seo_question: What is the Shia supplication for healing by invoking the Jinn's obedience to Imam Ali?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi illustrates the Shia concept of *tawassul* through the spiritual authority (*sultan*) of Imam Ali, specifically referencing his encounter with the Jinn of Wadi al-Sabratah. The supplication employs a formula of binding (*'azama*) that links the immediate affliction to the Jinn's prior obedience, ensuring the patient's swift recovery through the same divine mandate. It highlights the practical application of Imam Ali's intercessory power in healing rituals within the Imami tradition.
